content.text:
droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `process_death` (process_death): Fill the screen's form, let Android kill the app in the background, then come back to it.
Steps: [{"fill": true}, {"fault": "kill_in_background"}, {"fault": "relaunch"}, {"settle": 6}]
Result: lost_state: 6 of 6 filled fields changed or emptied
Fields lost (before -> after): {'field_name': ['Ravi Kumar', ''], 'field_email': ['ravi@example.com', ''], 'field_phone': ['9876543210', ''], 'field_address': ['12 MG Road', ''], 'field_city': ['Bengaluru', ''], 'field_pincode': ['560001', '']}

## Diagnosis
Root cause: The checkout form's six fields are plain `mutableStateOf` properties on `CheckoutViewModel` (CheckoutViewModel.kt:14-19), and the ViewModel has no `SavedStateHandle` or any other persistence. CheckoutScreen binds each field directly to `vm.name`, `vm.email`, etc. (CheckoutScreen.kt:67-72). When Android kills the process in the background, the ViewModel and its in-memory state are destroyed. On relaunch, the route is restored via `rememberSaveable` (MainActivity.kt:62), so the user lands back on Checkout, but `viewModel()` creates a fresh `CheckoutViewModel` with every field blank. The route survives process death, but the form data does not.
Fix approach: Back the form state with `SavedStateHandle`: take `SavedStateHandle` in the ViewModel constructor and implement each field as `savedStateHandle.getStateFlow` or `savedStateHandle.mutableStateOf` (for example `var name by savedStateHandle.saveable { mutableStateOf("") }` from `androidx.compose.runtime.saveable`), so values are written to the saved-state bundle and restored after process death. The default `viewModel()` factory supplies a SavedStateHandle automatically, so the call site can stay unchanged. Alternatively, use `rememberSaveable` for each field in the composable, but the ViewModel approach keeps the state alongside the placeOrder logic.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:13-19 - ViewModel with no constructor arguments; six fields stored as plain mutableStateOf with no saved-state backing; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:1-10 - no SavedStateHandle import or usage anywhere in the ViewModel; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:34 - `vm: CheckoutViewModel = viewModel()` creates a fresh ViewModel with default state when the process is restored; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:67-72 - each OutlinedTextField is bound directly to a ViewModel property, so the UI shows whatever the ViewModel holds, which is blank after restore; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/MainActivity.kt:62 - the route is saved with rememberSaveable, so the user returns to the checkout screen but the form data is not restored; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/MainActivity.kt:80 - CheckoutScreen is reached via the restored route, confirming the screen comes back while its state is lost

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt

## Regression test
Add a JVM unit test `CheckoutViewModelProcessDeathTest` in src/test. Create `CheckoutViewModel(SavedStateHandle())`, set name/email/phone/address/city/pincode to known values, then copy the handle's saved state into a new `SavedStateHandle` (simulating restore after process death) and construct a second `CheckoutViewModel` with it. Assert that all six fields in the second instance equal the originals and that `isComplete` is true. Before the fix, the no-arg ViewModel does not compile against a SavedStateHandle constructor, or the restored fields are empty, so the test fails. After the fix, it passes.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

package com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui

import androidx.lifecycle.SavedStateHandle
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test

class CheckoutViewModelProcessDeathTest {
    @Test
    fun formFieldsSurviveProcessDeath() {
        val handle = SavedStateHandle()
        val original = CheckoutViewModel(handle).apply {
            name = "Ravi Kumar"
            email = "ravi@example.com"
            phone = "9876543210"
            address = "12 MG Road"
            city = "Bengaluru"
            pincode = "560001"
        }

        val restoredHandle = SavedStateHandle(handle.keys().associateWith { handle.get<Any?>(it) })
        val restored = CheckoutViewModel(restoredHandle)

        assertEquals(original.name, restored.name)
        assertEquals(original.email, restored.email)
        assertEquals(original.phone, restored.phone)
        assertEquals(original.address, restored.address)
        assertEquals(original.city, restored.city)
        assertEquals(original.pincode, restored.pincode)
        assertEquals("Ravi Kumar", restored.name)
        assertTrue(restored.isComplete)
    }
}

content.text: I changed `CheckoutViewModel` so the six checkout form fields are backed by a `SavedStateHandle`. It now takes the handle in its constructor, so the default `viewModel()` call in `CheckoutScreen` works unchanged. Each field reads its starting value from the handle and writes every edit back to it, so the form is restored after process death. `CheckoutScreen.kt` needed no edits. I haven't compiled or run anything, because I had no shell tool here, so please run the test yourself. The regression test is `CheckoutViewModelProcessDeathTest`, in `app/src/test/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/`. It fills all six fields, copies the handle's keys and values into a new `SavedStateHandle`, and builds a second ViewModel from it. It then asserts all six fields match and `isComplete` is true. It fails to compile against the old no-argument ViewModel. It copies the keys and values directly instead of using `saveState()`, because `saveState()` needs `Bundle`, which isn't available in JVM unit tests.
